title: Physical Streaming Replication
description: Architect primary-standby streaming replication, synchronous vs asynchronous replication, and replication slots.

data.text: **Physical Streaming Replication** streams raw Write-Ahead Log (WAL) records byte-for-byte from a primary database to one or more standby read-replicas. Replicas replay the WAL stream, maintaining an exact binary replica of the primary cluster.

rows: Primary commits immediately; streams WAL in background.
Small window of data loss if primary dies before replica receives WAL.
Primary waits until at least one standby confirms WAL receipt before returning success to client.
Adds network roundtrip latency to every transaction commit.

data.title: Always Use Replication Slots
data.text: A **Replication Slot** instructs the primary server not to delete archived WAL files until the replica has acknowledged replaying them, preventing 'WAL segment already removed' errors.

A physical replica is created with `pg_basebackup`, which copies the data directory and configures the standby to stream WAL. On the primary, a replication slot guarantees the WAL the replica still needs is retained even if the replica disconnects.

data.title: Create a replication slot and a standby
data.content: The slot is created on the primary; `pg_basebackup` then clones the data directory and starts streaming. The `-R` flag writes the connection settings automatically.
data.code:
# On the primary: create a slot so WAL is retained for this replica
psql -h primary -c "SELECT * FROM pg_create_physical_replication_slot('replica1_slot');"

# On the standby host: clone the primary and start streaming
pg_basebackup \
  -h primary \
  -D /var/lib/postgresql/16/main \
  -U replicator \
  -Fp -Xs -P -R \
  -S replica1_slot

# Verify replication is streaming
psql -h primary -c "SELECT client_addr, state, sync_state, replay_lag FROM pg_stat_replication;"

data.title: Watch for replica lag and slot bloat
data.text: Replication slots prevent WAL removal, which is exactly what you want for a healthy replica — but if a replica goes away permanently and its slot is not dropped, the primary's disk fills with WAL and eventually stops accepting writes. Monitor `pg_replication_slots` for a growing `pg_wal_lsn_diff` and drop abandoned slots. Query `pg_stat_replication.replay_lag` to catch a replica falling behind before it becomes an outage.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Streaming replication creates exact binary read replicas.
Use replication slots to prevent replicas from falling behind and breaking.
Synchronous replication guarantees zero data loss at the cost of commit latency.
